prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name a single “best” interior painter for St. Louis (companies change, and “best” depends on your needs). I can, however, help you find the right one and evaluate candidates. If you want, tell me your zip code, project size, budget, and timeline and I can narrow recommendations or help compare quotes.

In the meantime, here’s a practical plan and tools to find the best painter for your job:

1) Where to look
- Google and Google Maps (look at overall rating + recent reviews)
- Yelp and Angi (formerly Angie’s List)
- Better Business Bureau (complaints, accreditation)
- Local Facebook groups / Nextdoor recommendations
- Ask neighbors/homeowners for referrals and to see finished work in person

2) What matters (your decision criteria)
- Quality of prep work (patching, sanding, priming)
- Paint brands and number of coats
- Crew skill and whether the company uses employees vs. day labor/subcontractors
- Written estimate and scope of work
- Proof of insurance (liability + workers’ comp)
- Warranty/guarantee on workmanship
- Communication, punctuality, and cleanup
- Portfolio and references

3) Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see certificates?
- Do you provide a written estimate and contract? What’s included/excluded?
- Which paint brand/products will you use and how many coats?
- How will surfaces be prepared and repaired?
- Who will do the work — your employees or subcontractors?
- What is the timeline and who is the point of contact?
- Can you provide references and photos of recent similar projects?
- What’s your payment schedule and warranty?

4) Red flags
- Very low bids compared to others
- Cash-only, no written contract, or request for full payment up front
- No insurance or unwillingness to provide proof
- Poor communication or inability to provide references/portfolio
- Rushed or incomplete prep work described

5) Typical cost estimates (very approximate)
- Small room (10x12): $300–$800
- Whole interior of an average 2,000 sq ft house: $3,000–$10,000+
Prices vary by paint quality, number of coats, amount of prep, trim work, ceilings, and local labor rates. Get at least 3 detailed bids.

6) Sample message to send to painters
Hi — I’m getting quotes for interior painting for [brief description: e.g., 2 bedrooms + hallway, 900 sq ft, walls and trim]. Please send a written estimate that includes scope (prep, number of coats, paint brand), timeline, proof of insurance, and references for similar recent jobs. Thank you — [Your name and phone].

If you want, give me:
- your zip code
- a short project description (rooms/sq ft, walls + trim or ceilings too, current condition)
I’ll suggest the best ways to get local quotes and can help evaluate any estimates you receive.
